findings: Captured NextNameBlock137e900, GrowShard1385450 and ReinsertSlot138a040 and verified all16 code spans against the current live executable. Conditional insertion preserves original name bytes while lookup folds ASCII only, writes encoded block/offset and Number separately, and reuses an existing identity on repeat/case-alias lookup.

Isolated synthetic pool starts with a None entry and256 eight-slot shards. Real native construction/hash/lookup/insertion/growth/rehash instructions execute; only generic allocation/free/copy/fill, imported locks and cookie checks are substituted. Heap/table frees unmap pages; emulated writes are restricted to explicitly modeled storage.

Actual growth entries satisfy10*new_count>9*old_capacity and request twice the old slot capacity. Native rehash redistributes existing full slot values through real hash preparation; all prior identities and count/slot population survive.

Long narrow and wide names trigger actual native name-block rollover. All fresh input entries preserve header width, original bytes and suffix Number. ASCII aliases reuse identity, while selected non-ASCII letter pairs remain distinct.
limits: Results are conditional on successful, correctly aligned allocation and correct copy/fill/free primitives. Client allocator, memory failure, lock implementation, concurrency, initialization and fatal-limit behavior are not certified.

Synthetic fixtures do not demonstrate real client insertion history or live callbacks. No live process writes/functions/locks are used. Rehash batching is exercised by fixtures, not exhaustively proved for every valid table.
This is FName infrastructure evidence, not a full card-effect audit or a general production name resolver. Canonical blacklist input contract and simulator kernel behavior remain unchanged.
